messages:
observability-bot: ALERT kv_reuse_mismatch spike in prod-eu-west-1. rule triggered at 3305559999. affected shards: model-gptx-v2 shard 7..12.
incidents-bot: incident INC-33055 created (sev=2) — paging oncall SRE and eng-runtime. https://redwood.incidents/INC-33055
noor: oncall SRE here, looking at dashboards. reuse_mismatch jumped 0.3% -> 5.9% across several workers. latency climb on continuous-batching clusters.
alin: can you paste the log excerpts for seq_expected/seq_seen?
noor: sample log from worker-7:
```
2026-03-17T02:46:23Z worker-7 WARN kv_store: reuse_mismatch seq_expected=3421 seq_seen=3389 key=page/model_gptx-v2/layer12/chunk3
2026-03-17T02:46:23Z worker-7 ERROR generate: duplicate_token detected prefix=8 dup_len=4
```
zach: seq gap ~32. that pattern matches stale reuse pointer (paged rehydrate race). did any paging/backing-store or batching flags change in the last 24h?
noor: there was an autoscale experiment for continuous-batcher in eu that increased max_batch_ms and enabled aggressive coalescing.
devops-bot: note: recent config change recorded: continuous-batcher.autoscale=aggressive at 2026-03-16T21:10Z in eu regions.
alin: reproduce locally: when two inflight requests are coalesced and a paged segment is rehydrated concurrently, update_reuse_pointer runs without the page mutex -> another request reads half-updated pointer -> later rehydrate/fill returns the old page leading to wrong seq offsets. root cause candidate: missing lock / atomic update during paged_store::rehydrate() pointer write.
noor: immediate mitigations proposed: 1) disable kv reuse fast-path via FF in affected regions, 2) throttle continuous-batcher to reduce coalescing (max_batch_ms=10), 3) targeted restarts of nodes with seq_drift>8, 4) evict page-index cache for affected model versions. which to execute first?
zach: do FF canary first (20%), then escalate. prepare evict command and restart list.
noor: issuing FF canary now: `redwoodctl ff set kv_reuse_fastpath=false --region eu-west-1 --pct 20`
incidents-bot: feature flag change recorded by noor (canary 20%).
noor: applying continuous-batcher override for region eu-west-1: `redwoodctl config set continuous-batcher.max_batch_ms=10 --region eu-west-1`
devops-bot: config change applied.
zach: running targeted restart on nodes with seq_drift>8:
```
for id in $(redwoodctl nodes list --region eu-west-1 --filter "seq_drift>8"); do redwoodctl node restart $id; done
```
noor: evicting page-index cache for model gptx-v2 in eu-west-1:
```
redwoodctl kv-cache evict --model gptx-v2 --type page-index --region eu-west-1
```
cs-lina: CS report: three enterprise customers observed token duplication and misordered fragments. two opened priority tickets. customer impact window estimated ~14m.
alin: metrics after 8m of 20% canary: reuse_mismatch down ~75% in canary nodes, non-canary shards still elevated. proceeding to 60% rollout.
noor: FF at 60% (14:58Z). monitoring shows region-wide improvement, but a small tail of duplicates remains on older worker ids.
zach: while FF is rolling, add a lightweight runtime guard that forces full KV reload for any request that observes seq_gap>12. small change, low risk, can be hotfixed. who can land quick patch?
alin: I can prepare a hotfix: runtime/guards: if seq_gap>12 then reload_kv_for_request() and emit metric reuse_gap_forced_reload. will push hotfix tag hotfix/kv-gap-2026-03-17-1.
noor: canary hotfix deploy starting now.
incidents-bot: hotfix deployed to canary at 3305560199 by alin.
noor: canary hotfix shows immediate suppression of token duplication for the few stubborn workers. rolling hotfix to full region.
zach: long-term fix: wrap paged_store::rehydrate pointer updates with page_lock and perform atomic barrier + add unit + stress tests that simulate concurrent rehydrates with heavy coalescing. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4758
alin: PR also contains an integration test that runs 50 concurrent requests with randomized spills + simulated backing-store latency to exercise the race.
noor: customer communication: CS drafted note acknowledging degraded outputs and describing mitigation steps; sent to affected customers at 03:12Z, two customers confirmed improvement within 25m.
cs-lina: XCorp says outputs look normal; YCorp still sees occasional duplication but much reduced. escalated for deeper token diff capture.
incidents-bot: operational metrics: incident severity downgraded to sev=3 at 3305560399.
noor: add telemetry items: reuse_pointer_write_latency, reuse_pointer_conflicts, seq_gap_count. add alert for token_duplication_rate > 0.5% per 5m.
zach: ops items: gate future batching-autoscale experiments with canary that includes KV reuse stress tests. schedule a mandatory checklist item for paged-store changes review.
alin: landed hotfix and FF fully rolled by 3305560499. reuse_mismatch back to baseline.
noor: postmortem plan: 45m postmortem tomorrow with eng-runtime, eng-ml, eng-sre, cs, product. include replay of logs, timeline, RCA, and rollout plan for PR 4758.
cs-lina: leaving follow-up tickets: CS-12345 (customer follow-ups), INF-6789 (RCA + patch tracking).
noor: oncall handoff: I'll post a short summary and links to commands, logs, PR, and evict commands in #oncall-handoff. next oncall please monitor reuse_mismatch, token_duplication, and seq_gap_count for 48h.
incidents-bot: incident INC-33055 resolved (ops) at 3305560599 — follow-up RCA assigned: https://redwood.incidents/INC-33055/rca
